Emergency services templates: a ready-made set for private emergency and response control rooms (medical, armed response, roadside help, panic buttons). It brings always-open queues, an emergency line with no menu that goes straight to controllers, a non-emergency line with a short menu, incident tickets with their own fields and priority rules, the Control room wallboard and daily answer-time and incident reports. A worked example in Help and in the administrators' course walks through setting one up. The templates are not a public emergency-number system; they say when to hand a caller to the state's numbers.

Dropped callers called back: on any call flow, Call back callers who hang up while waiting puts a callback in the same queue at once, marked Dropped call, so the next free agent calls them back.

Caller location by link: an agent can send a caller a link that shares their position once, for that call only. The location and a map appear on the desk and the ticket within seconds; the link works for an hour and nothing about the caller's phone is kept.

Moya: connect your organisation's Moya number, South Africa's data-free messaging app. People who chat to it arrive under Chats on the desk like any other channel, and you can message customers on Moya by their mobile number without them using data. Is this number on Moya? on the customer shows whether they can be reached there, STOP is honoured, and Moya appears in broadcasts, contact journeys and the reports.

Users: a Search by name or email box above the list finds people across the whole tenant. Capitals make no difference and the likeliest matches come first.

Fixes: a caller waiting in a queue with hold music can press 1 for a callback again; reloading the desk or opening it in a second tab no longer counts as signing in somewhere else."}
